title: A separated switch says what it is, instead of Box 7
goal: Take a settings pane apart and the words on it come back as layers wearing those words, which is what makes the list searchable. Everything that is not words comes back as Box 1 through Box 10, in one flat run: a card, a button, a switch and a text field all get the same name and a number. Somebody redlining that pane wants the switch next to Launch at login, and the only way to find it is to click boxes until the right one lights up. The pieces that are not text should be as findable as the pieces that are.
notes:
From the focus-feature review in the 2026-09-18 digest, on queue/audits/2026-09-18-separate-into-layers.json. That audit's own evaluate list asks it twice: 'The switches and fields are called Box 5 to Box 10. Is a numbered box findable, when the runs of text next to them wear the words they say?' and 'The pill says 10 boxes, but looking at this pane you would probably count four'.

The runner who shipped the separation left this in the task log rather than filing it, calling it a naming question for the user. Filing it because the harm is not a matter of taste: the app already knows how to name a piece after words (it does it for every text run), and it declines to use that for the pieces sitting inside and beside those words, so half the list is unsearchable. If the shape of the answer turns out to need the user (for example whether a card should be called Card rather than Box), open a card for that specific choice rather than for the whole task.
acceptance: On Tests/PhotonzRenderTests/Fixtures/settings-pane-2x.png, separating the Background row gives a Layers list in which the switch beside a labelled row can be found from the list alone, without clicking pieces on the canvas to find out which is which
A piece that is not text takes its name from something a person can see: the words it sits beside or contains, or what it plainly is, with a numbered fallback only where nothing is available
The names are stable: separating the same picture twice gives the same names in the same order
The pill's count is explained by what the list shows, so somebody who counts four things on the pane and reads ten is not left guessing which six they missed
Searching the find field for a word on the pane reaches the piece beside it, not only the run of text itself
The four separate-* walks still pass, and one of them checks a name rather than only a count

Try it: Photonz Dev, release Next, next-separate-into-layers and next-layer-groups on. Open the fixture above, pick Background, run Separate into Layers, then find the Launch at login switch in the list
Audit under queue/audits/, and anything rough filed as a follow-up if it clears the bar or logged here if it does not

log.note: owns these walks: separated-boxes-say-their-words-walk, separate-boxes-walk, separate-hierarchy-walk, separate-shadow-walk, separate-whole-screenshot-walk

Adversarial review before building: the mock is a naming question, not a surface, so the only real risk was naming a piece after words that are not its own. Three guards came out of it and all three are in the rule: a box takes what is INSIDE it only when that is exactly one run and nothing else (so a card holding three labelled rows is named after none of them), it takes what is BESIDE it only from pieces sharing its container in the same LayerNesting tree the list is built from, and only across a gap nothing else on the row reaches into. Pairing DOWNWARDS (a field under its label) was cut on purpose: no pane in the walk set has that shape and it is the shape that would name a card after the heading above it. One run names at most one box, so a row with a label and two controls never comes back saying the same thing twice.

Built as a NAME WORKED OUT AS THE LIST IS DRAWN, not a rename: the box points at the picture of the words that name it (Layer.labelledBy, set by SeparatedBoxNames.labels as the pieces are built) and Layer.displayName(readWords:) turns that into "Launch at login box" when the background reading comes back. Same contract the words on a run of text already have: no undo step, no edit, gone the moment somebody types a name of their own. On the real fixture, end to end: eight of the ten boxes wear words (4 switches, 2 fields, 2 buttons) and the two cards keep Box 1 and Box 2.

Review of the built thing, on the probe: the Layout section was calling the picked group by its stored name while its own row said the new one ("Contents of Box 4" over a row reading "Save Changes box"), so ContentsSelection and PlacementInspector now name a container the way the layers list does. Left rough: the name column is about fourteen characters at the dock's resting width and cuts the TAIL, so "Play sound on capture box" reads as "Play sound on..." and looks like the row of words above it, with only the thumbnail telling them apart. Putting the word in front would survive the cut and turn the column back into a wall of Box, which is what this task was filed to end, so it stayed at the back and the audit asks the user about it directly.

The four separate-* walks all turn next-a-separated-row-says-its-words OFF, so none of them could ever check a worded name: they pass unchanged (separate-boxes, separate-hierarchy, separate-shadow, separate-whole-screenshot, all ok). The name check went into a new walk with the flag on, separated-boxes-say-their-words-walk: it separates the fixture, waits for the reading, double clicks the switch inside the card and asks what the list calls what it picked ("Launch at login box"), then clicks the button ("Save Changes box"), and undoes. It is lock-safe and photographed the real window four times.

Scripts/test.sh: 8308 tests, everything green except theDensePageStopsAtTheCeilingRatherThanHandingBackAWall, which is a PRE-EXISTING flake and not this change. Proved by stashing every local change and running it four times on clean main 258d7422: 359, pass, 355, pass. Filed as the-dense-page-counts-a-different-number-of-left with that reproduction.

Every separated piece that is not text now wears the words it sits inside or beside: "Launch at login box" for the switch on that row, "Save Changes box" for the button, with only the two cards keeping Box 1 and Box 2 because they hold three labelled rows each. The rule is SeparatedBoxNames in PhotonzCore (13 unit tests), the name is worked out as the list is drawn from Layer.labelledBy so it costs no undo step, and the find field reaches the boxes as well as the words. Verified end to end on the real fixture by SeparatedRowsSayTheirWordsTests and on the running app by the new separated-boxes-say-their-words-walk, which photographed the window four times; separate-boxes, separate-hierarchy, separate-shadow and separate-whole-screenshot all still pass. Audit: queue/audits/2026-09-18-separated-box-names.json. Shipped in fa49afce.
